Product / Retention

Monthly customer churn rate

The percentage of paying customer accounts present at the start of a month that cease to be paying customers by the end. This logo-based measure counts accounts rather than lost revenue or individual seats.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

The percentage of paying customer accounts present at the start of a month that cease to be paying customers by the end. This logo-based measure counts accounts rather than lost revenue or individual seats.

% / month

How we use it

We join billing status and customer history to examine churn by acquisition cohort, plan, and reason, then identify onboarding or service issues worth investigating.

Transparent calculationStarting-month paying customer accounts lost by month end ÷ paying customer accounts at month start × 100
starting paying accounts200
lost starting accounts10

10 ÷ 200 × 100 = 5% monthly churn from the starting customer cohort.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Starting paying account cohort
  • Plan and customer segment
  • Cancellation reason and tenure

Questions we investigate

  • Which starting accounts were actually lost?
  • Do cancellations reflect service or payment issues?
  • Are reactivations and account merges treated consistently?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Review reasons with customer-facing teams.
  • Improve onboarding and recovery for relevant issues.
  • Compare account churn with revenue retention.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Customer success and finance leads
Monthly for the fixed starting cohort.

Required data

  • Starting-month paying account IDs
  • Month-end account status and loss events
  • Account merge, pause, and reactivation rules

Read the measure with context

Zero starting accounts makes the rate undefined. New customers acquired during the month do not belong in this denominator. Define cancellation, grace-period, and reactivation rules consistently. Logo churn differs from revenue churn and from a provider's native subscription-churn policy.
